paragraphs.context: At this school, you will be learning side by side with dragons
paragraphs.mainIdea: A school for all the tribes.
paragraphs.simple: This page is a welcome letter from Jade Mountain Academy. Young dragons from all the tribes study there together, so the next pages give some facts about each tribe.

paragraphs.context: You have been assigned to a winglet with six other dragons;
paragraphs.mainIdea: Each student is in a winglet.
paragraphs.simple: Every student is put in a small class called a winglet, with six dragons from other tribes. The list of winglets comes on the next page.

background.note: At Jade Mountain Academy, a small class of seven dragonets, one from each tribe.

paragraphs.context: WE WISH YOU ALL THE POWER OF WINGS OF FIRE!
paragraphs.simple: The letter says the students are the hope for a long peace in Pyrrhia. It ends with a wish. "Wings of fire" is a phrase from the old Dragonet Prophecy; here it means "may you be strong and do great things".

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can survive a long time without water, poison enemies with the tips
paragraphs.simple: SandWings can live a long time without water. They can poison enemies with the end of their tail, like a scorpion, hide under the sand, and breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: since the end of the War of SandWing Succession, Queen Thorn
paragraphs.mainIdea: The SandWings have a new queen.
paragraphs.simple: There was a long war about who would be the SandWing queen. That war is over now, and Thorn is the queen.

background.note: The war that began when Queen Oasis died and her three daughters fought to be queen of the SandWings. Most of the tribes joined in.
Thorn is now queen of the SandWings.

paragraphs.context: Students at Jade Mountain: Arid, Onyx, Ostrich, Pronghorn, Qibli
paragraphs.simple: These are the five SandWing students at the school. Each tribe page ends with a list like this.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire (if warm enough), hold their breath for up
paragraphs.simple: MudWings can breathe fire when they are warm, stay under water or mud for an hour without breathing, and hide in mud. They are very strong.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: powerful fighters and fliers, can breathe fire
paragraphs.simple: SkyWings are strong fighters and fast fliers, and they can breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Queen Ruby (although some dragons still support Queen Scarlet,
paragraphs.simple: Ruby is the SkyWing queen now. But some SkyWings still want Scarlet, the old queen who lost her throne. Scarlet may still be alive and hiding somewhere.

background.note: Ruby is Queen Scarlet's daughter. After Scarlet loses her throne, Ruby becomes queen of the SkyWings.
Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.

paragraphs.context: Description: blue or green or aquamarine scales; webs between their claws; gills
paragraphs.simple: SeaWings are blue or green. They have skin between their claws, gills for breathing under water, and stripes that glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can withstand subzero temperatures and bright light, exhale a deadly frostbreath

sentences.simple: Watching Anemone go made Turtle feel as sick as the day he learned Scarlet's soldiers had caught his father.

parts.text: Turtle watched her go
parts.meaning: Turtle watched Anemone leave

parts.text: with the same sick, sinking feeling
parts.meaning: feeling just as sick and hopeless

parts.text: that had hit him the day he heard his father had been captured by Queen Scarlet’s troops.
parts.meaning: as on the day he heard Scarlet's soldiers had caught his father.

sentences.grammar: "That had hit him" describes the feeling. "Had been captured" is passive past perfect.

sentences.context: The truth was, he hadn’t just taken the scroll; he’d attacked Chameleon with it, bashing him in the face and probably breaking his nose.
sentences.simple: In fact, Turtle didn't only take the scroll; he hit Chameleon in the face with it and probably broke his nose.

parts.text: The truth was, he hadn’t just taken the scroll;
parts.meaning: Really, he didn't only take the scroll;

parts.text: he’d attacked Chameleon with it,
parts.meaning: he had attacked Chameleon with it,

parts.text: bashing him in the face and probably breaking his nose.
parts.meaning: hitting him in the face and probably breaking his nose.

sentences.grammar: The semicolon joins two linked ideas. "Not just… ; …" shows the second fact is worse.

sentences.context: But he managed to stay put, sinking into a crouch, and so he was watching as Darkstalker lifted a claw to gently touch the earring in his ear, pale against the black scales.
sentences.simple: Turtle stayed where he was, crouching, so he saw Darkstalker touch the pale earring in his ear.

parts.text: But he managed to stay put,
parts.meaning: But he stayed where he was,

parts.text: sinking into a crouch,
parts.meaning: crouching low,

parts.text: and so he was watching as Darkstalker lifted a claw to gently touch the earring in his ear,
parts.meaning: so he saw Darkstalker gently touch the earring in his ear,

parts.text: pale against the black scales.
parts.meaning: which looked pale against his black scales.

sentences.grammar: "Managed to" means "was able to, with effort". "As" means "at the moment when".

sentences.context: Every once in a while Darkstalker would pass her a scroll and ask her to read it out loud to him, or to check it for references to Fathom, and she would do so, beaming.
sentences.simple: Sometimes Darkstalker gave Anemone a scroll to read aloud or to search for Fathom's name, and she happily did it.

parts.text: Every once in a while
parts.meaning: Sometimes

parts.text: Darkstalker would pass her a scroll and ask her to read it out loud to him, or to check it for references to Fathom,
parts.meaning: Darkstalker gave her a scroll and asked her to read it aloud, or to look for Fathom in it,

parts.text: and she would do so, beaming.
parts.meaning: and she did it, smiling happily.

sentences.grammar: "Would + verb" describes repeated past actions. "Do so" means "do that".

sentences.context: Soon they came back through the cave, all of them with relieved expressions, knowing that Scarlet was dead and Ruby was safely their queen for certain now.
sentences.simple: The SkyWings came back looking relieved, because they now knew Scarlet was dead and Ruby was surely their queen.

parts.text: Soon they came back through the cave,
parts.meaning: Soon they walked back through the cave,

parts.text: all of them with relieved expressions,
parts.meaning: all looking relieved,

parts.text: knowing that Scarlet was dead and Ruby was safely their queen for certain now.
parts.meaning: because they knew Scarlet was dead and Ruby was definitely their queen.

sentences.grammar: "Knowing that…" gives the reason for their relief.

sentences.context: From his position, he could just see a sliver of the cave beyond: Stonemover’s gray, fossilized arm; a tangle of NightWing tails; a pool of blood slowly creeping across the stone floor.
sentences.simple: From where he was, Turtle could see a small part of the cave: Stonemover's stone arm, some tails, and blood spreading on the floor.

parts.text: From his position,
parts.meaning: From where he was,

parts.text: he could just see a sliver of the cave beyond:
parts.meaning: he could see only a thin piece of the cave:

parts.text: Stonemover’s gray, fossilized arm; a tangle of NightWing tails; a pool of blood slowly creeping across the stone floor.
parts.meaning: Stonemover's gray stone arm; many NightWing tails; blood slowly spreading over the floor.

sentences.grammar: The colon introduces a list. The semicolons separate the list items.

sentences.context: He couldn’t imagine willingly fossilizing himself … but he looked down at his clenched talons and wondered what he would do to stop them from hurting anyone.
sentences.simple: Turtle couldn't imagine turning himself to stone on purpose, but he looked at his tight claws and wondered what he would do to stop them hurting others.

parts.text: He couldn’t imagine willingly fossilizing himself …
parts.meaning: He couldn't picture turning himself to stone on purpose …

parts.text: but he looked down at his clenched talons
parts.meaning: but he looked at his tight claws

parts.text: and wondered what he would do to stop them from hurting anyone.
parts.meaning: and asked himself what he would do to keep them from hurting anyone.

sentences.grammar: "Stop… from + -ing" means prevent something.

sentences.context: So when one of them did something wrong — and if someone was paying attention to them long enough to notice — their punishment was almost always isolation.
sentences.simple: When one of the princes did something wrong, and if anyone even noticed, he was usually punished by being left alone.

parts.text: So when one of them did something wrong
parts.meaning: So when a prince did something bad

parts.text: — and if someone was paying attention to them long enough to notice —
parts.meaning: (and if anyone watched them long enough to see it)

parts.text: their punishment was almost always isolation.
parts.meaning: they were nearly always punished by being kept alone.

sentences.grammar: The part between dashes adds a second condition. "Isolation" means being alone.

sentences.context: From the first night, they had dragged their reed mats together and slept back to back, feeling as if the world was really still there as long as there were other scales close by.
sentences.simple: From the first night, Turtle and Umber pushed their mats together and slept back to back, feeling safe with someone close.

parts.text: From the first night,
parts.meaning: Starting on the first night,

parts.text: they had dragged their reed mats together and slept back to back,
parts.meaning: they pulled their sleeping mats together and slept back to back,

parts.text: feeling as if the world was really still there as long as there were other scales close by.
parts.meaning: feeling that the world was all right as long as another dragon was near.

sentences.grammar: "As if" introduces a feeling. "As long as" means "if, and only while".

sentences.context: If Darkstalker can tell when an animus casts a spell, Turtle realized, his heart floundering wildly around in his chest, then I can never use my magic again.
sentences.simple: Turtle realized with a pounding heart that if Darkstalker can sense spells, he can never use magic again.

parts.text: If Darkstalker can tell when an animus casts a spell,
parts.meaning: If Darkstalker can sense every spell,

parts.text: Turtle realized, his heart floundering wildly around in his chest,
parts.meaning: Turtle understood, with his heart beating wildly,

parts.text: then I can never use my magic again.
parts.meaning: then I can't ever use magic again.

sentences.grammar: Turtle's thought is in the present tense ("can"), but "realized" is past. "If… then…" shows condition and result.

sentences.context: In detective stories, it was all right for one of the partners to be incompetent and unreliable, because the other one would make up for it.
sentences.simple: In detective stories, one partner can be bad at the job, because the other partner covers for them.

parts.text: In detective stories,
parts.meaning: In stories about detectives,

parts.text: it was all right for one of the partners to be incompetent and unreliable,
parts.meaning: one partner could be unskilled and not dependable,

parts.text: because the other one would make up for it.
parts.meaning: because the other one would fix that.

sentences.grammar: "It was all right for… to…" means it was OK. "Make up for" means balance something bad.

sentences.context: But the smell here was nothing like the ocean: wild fruit and monkey droppings, heat and rich dirt, and roots growing in thick tangles in place of fish, salt, wide open air.
sentences.simple: The rainforest smelled completely different from the sea: fruit, monkey dung, heat, dirt and roots instead of fish, salt and open air.

parts.text: But the smell here was nothing like the ocean:
parts.meaning: But it didn't smell at all like the sea:

parts.text: wild fruit and monkey droppings, heat and rich dirt, and roots growing in thick tangles
parts.meaning: wild fruit, monkey poo, heat, dark soil and tangled roots

parts.text: in place of fish, salt, wide open air.
parts.meaning: instead of fish, salt and open air.

sentences.grammar: "Nothing like" means "not at all like". "In place of" means "instead of".

sentences.context: He dropped from the hot-sun sky down and down into dappled green light that reminded him of the Summer Palace, before it was destroyed.
sentences.simple: Turtle flew down from the hot sky into spotted green light that reminded him of the Summer Palace before it was destroyed.
sentences.main: The forest reminds Turtle of home.

parts.text: He dropped from the hot-sun sky down and down
parts.meaning: He flew lower and lower from the hot, sunny sky

parts.text: into dappled green light
parts.meaning: into spotted green light

parts.text: that reminded him of the Summer Palace, before it was destroyed.
parts.meaning: which made him think of the Summer Palace before it was ruined.

sentences.grammar: "Dappled" means with spots of light and shadow. "That reminded him" describes the light.

sentences.context: Glory didn’t stop him; she was staring at Darkstalker as though he’d upended eighty million words on her head and she was trying to put them in the right order to make a scroll.
sentences.simple: Glory let Deathbringer speak; she stared at Darkstalker as if she were trying to make sense of a huge pile of words.

parts.text: Glory didn’t stop him;
parts.meaning: Glory let him speak;

parts.text: she was staring at Darkstalker
parts.meaning: she was looking hard at Darkstalker

parts.text: as though he’d upended eighty million words on her head
parts.meaning: as if he had dropped a huge number of words on her head

parts.text: and she was trying to put them in the right order to make a scroll.
parts.meaning: and she was trying to put them in order.

sentences.grammar: "As though" introduces an imaginary comparison. "Upended" means turned over and emptied.

sentences.context: If Albatross somehow came back to life, and he acted like a sane, friendly dragon, and Turtle had to choose between him or, say, Queen Glacier to rule the Kingdom of the Sea … who would he pick?
sentences.simple: Turtle imagines: if a friendly Albatross came back and he had to choose between him and an outsider queen like Glacier, whom would he choose?

parts.text: If Albatross somehow came back to life,
parts.meaning: If Albatross came back to life,

parts.text: and he acted like a sane, friendly dragon,
parts.meaning: and seemed normal and friendly,

parts.text: and Turtle had to choose between him or, say, Queen Glacier to rule the Kingdom of the Sea …
parts.meaning: and Turtle had to choose him or, for example, Queen Glacier as ruler of the sea …

parts.text: who would he pick?
parts.meaning: whom would he choose?

sentences.grammar: This is an imaginary condition: "If + past tense…, would…?" "Say" here means "for example".

sentences.context: Whenever he felt a little sick or too tired for anatomy class or needed help finding something, he’d reach for a magical solution — as long as it was small enough for no one to notice.
sentences.simple: When Turtle felt sick or tired or lost something, he used magic, but only small spells nobody would notice.

parts.text: Whenever he felt a little sick or too tired for anatomy class or needed help finding something,
parts.meaning: Every time he felt sick, too tired for class, or couldn't find something,

parts.text: he’d reach for a magical solution
parts.meaning: he would use magic to fix it

parts.text: — as long as it was small enough for no one to notice.
parts.meaning: — but only if it was small enough that nobody noticed.

sentences.grammar: "He'd" means "he would" (a past habit). "As long as" means "only if".

sentences.context: His claws felt too big and awkward to work the catch open far enough and the earrings kept slipping out of his grasp and floating slowly down to the seaweed-carpeted floor of his room.
sentences.simple: Turtle's claws were too clumsy to open the earring, and it kept slipping and floating down to the floor.
sentences.main: Turtle can't put on the earring.

parts.text: His claws felt too big and awkward to work the catch open far enough
parts.meaning: His claws were too big and clumsy to open the clasp

parts.text: and the earrings kept slipping out of his grasp
parts.meaning: and the earrings kept falling from his claws

parts.text: and floating slowly down to the seaweed-carpeted floor of his room.
parts.meaning: and sinking slowly to the seaweed floor.

sentences.grammar: "Too… to…" means so much that something is impossible. "Kept + -ing" means again and again.

sentences.context: Turtle could end up as the only dragon in Pyrrhia who saw Darkstalker the way he really was — and then what?
sentences.simple: Turtle might be the only dragon who sees what Darkstalker is really like, and then what would he do?

parts.text: Turtle could end up as the only dragon in Pyrrhia
parts.meaning: Turtle might be the only dragon in Pyrrhia

parts.text: who saw Darkstalker the way he really was
parts.meaning: who saw what Darkstalker was truly like

parts.text: — and then what?
parts.meaning: — and what would happen then?

sentences.grammar: "End up" means be in a situation at the end. "And then what?" is a short worried question.

sentences.context: He shuddered, and his hold on the coral loosened, and it darted forward in a flash and bopped Queen Glory on the side of her tail.
sentences.simple: Turtle shivered and loosened his grip, and the coral shot forward and tapped Glory's tail.

parts.text: He shuddered,
parts.meaning: He shivered,

parts.text: and his hold on the coral loosened,
parts.meaning: and he held the coral less tightly,

parts.text: and it darted forward in a flash and bopped Queen Glory on the side of her tail.
parts.meaning: and it shot forward fast and tapped Queen Glory's tail.

sentences.grammar: Three actions are joined with "and". "Bopped" means hit lightly.

sentences.context: He looked up and saw colors rising slowly into the scales all across Kinkajou’s back, like the time he’d spilled five different ink bottles over his blank scroll, back when he still dreamed of being a writer.
sentences.simple: Turtle saw colors spreading slowly over Kinkajou's back, like the time he spilled five inks on a scroll when he wanted to be a writer.

parts.text: He looked up and saw colors rising slowly into the scales all across Kinkajou’s back,
parts.meaning: He looked up and saw colors slowly appearing on Kinkajou's back,

parts.text: like the time he’d spilled five different ink bottles over his blank scroll,
parts.meaning: like when he spilled five bottles of ink on an empty scroll,

parts.text: back when he still dreamed of being a writer.
parts.meaning: in the days when he wanted to be a writer.

sentences.grammar: "Like the time…" compares with a memory. "Back when" means "in the past, when".

sentences.context: When it finally crashed to earth, far below them, it was a massive, dense cube of some unfamiliar material, with no windows.
sentences.simple: When the branch hit the ground, it had become a huge, solid block of strange material with no windows.

parts.text: When it finally crashed to earth,
parts.meaning: When it finally hit the ground,

parts.text: far below them,
parts.meaning: a long way below them,

parts.text: it was a massive, dense cube of some unfamiliar material, with no windows.
parts.meaning: it was a huge, solid block made of something strange, without windows.

sentences.grammar: "It" means the branch. "Some unfamiliar material" means a material nobody knew.

sentences.context: He’d read enough scrolls to know that no heroic quest was ever that easy — but he’d also spent enough time with Kinkajou to realize that it wouldn’t do any good to tell her that.
sentences.simple: Turtle knew from books that quests are never easy, but he also knew telling Kinkajou wouldn't help.

parts.text: He’d read enough scrolls to know that no heroic quest was ever that easy
parts.meaning: He had read enough to know that quests are never so easy

parts.text: — but he’d also spent enough time with Kinkajou
parts.meaning: — but he also knew Kinkajou well enough

parts.text: to realize that it wouldn’t do any good to tell her that.
parts.meaning: to see that telling her would not help.

sentences.grammar: "Enough… to…" shows a result. "It wouldn't do any good" means "it would not help".

sentences.context: He stood on Glory’s platform, counting the supplies gathered below him, as NightWings gradually filled the clearing in whispering clumps of twos and threes.
sentences.simple: Darkstalker stood on the platform counting the food while NightWings slowly arrived in small whispering groups.

parts.text: He stood on Glory’s platform,
parts.meaning: Darkstalker stood on Glory's stage,

parts.text: counting the supplies gathered below him,
parts.meaning: counting the supplies below him,

parts.text: as NightWings gradually filled the clearing in whispering clumps of twos and threes.
parts.meaning: while NightWings slowly filled the clearing in small whispering groups.

sentences.grammar: "As" means "while". "Clumps of twos and threes" means small groups.

sentences.context: Whereas if Darkstalker caught Moon and Kinkajou trailing after him in the middle of the night, there would be some explaining to do, insignificance spell or no insignificance spell.
sentences.simple: But if Darkstalker caught Moon and Kinkajou following him at night, they would have to explain, even with Kinkajou's spell.

parts.text: Whereas if Darkstalker caught Moon and Kinkajou trailing after him in the middle of the night,
parts.meaning: But if Darkstalker found Moon and Kinkajou following him at night,

parts.text: there would be some explaining to do,
parts.meaning: they would have to explain,

parts.text: insignificance spell or no insignificance spell.
parts.meaning: with or without the insignificance spell.

sentences.grammar: "Whereas" shows a contrast. "X or no X" means "whether there is X or not".

sentences.context: At one point, as they flew over land that began sloping up into hills, Turtle felt a sudden buzzing shock, like he’d accidentally grabbed a baby electric eel.
sentences.simple: As they flew over the hills, Turtle suddenly felt a buzzing shock, like touching a small electric eel.
sentences.main: Something strange is in the hills.

parts.text: At one point,
parts.meaning: At one moment,

parts.text: as they flew over land that began sloping up into hills,
parts.meaning: while they flew over land that rose into hills,

parts.text: Turtle felt a sudden buzzing shock,
parts.meaning: Turtle suddenly felt a buzzing shock,

parts.text: like he’d accidentally grabbed a baby electric eel.
parts.meaning: as if he had touched a small electric fish.

sentences.grammar: "Like he'd…" is an informal way to say "as if he had…".

sentences.context: She needed to see him as bad and dangerous so that she’d help Kinkajou when the time came for whatever heroics were necessary.
sentences.simple: Turtle wanted Moon to think Darkstalker was bad so she would help Kinkajou when it was time to act.
sentences.main: Turtle keeps a secret from Moon.

parts.text: She needed to see him as bad and dangerous
parts.meaning: Moon had to think he was bad and dangerous

parts.text: so that she’d help Kinkajou
parts.meaning: so she would help Kinkajou

parts.text: when the time came for whatever heroics were necessary.
parts.meaning: when they needed to do something brave.

sentences.grammar: "So that" shows purpose. "Whatever heroics" means "any brave actions".

sentences.context: They watched the NightWings gather in the sky like storm clouds until the tribe finally wheeled away west, and then Turtle, Moon, and Kinkajou lifted off and followed them.
sentences.simple: They watched the NightWings gather and fly west, and then the three friends took off after them.

parts.text: They watched the NightWings gather in the sky like storm clouds
parts.meaning: They watched the NightWings gather in the sky like dark clouds

parts.text: until the tribe finally wheeled away west,
parts.meaning: until the tribe turned and flew west,

parts.text: and then Turtle, Moon, and Kinkajou lifted off and followed them.
parts.meaning: and then the three friends took off and followed.

sentences.grammar: "Until" tells when the watching stopped. "Wheeled" means turned in a curve.

sentences.context: If it did, maybe it would be a good thing — maybe it would help Turtle get Moon away from Darkstalker’s influence.
sentences.simple: If the spell worked, it might be good, because it could help free Moon from Darkstalker.
sentences.main: Turtle sees a possible good side.

parts.text: If it did,
parts.meaning: If the spell worked,

parts.text: maybe it would be a good thing
parts.meaning: perhaps that would be good

parts.text: — maybe it would help Turtle get Moon away from Darkstalker’s influence.
parts.meaning: — perhaps it would help Turtle free Moon from Darkstalker's power.

sentences.grammar: "If it did" is short for "if it did work". The dash explains why.

sentences.context: If that was true, the same thing could be happening to Anemone that happened to Albatross, their murderous ancestor all those centuries ago.
sentences.simple: If so, Anemone might be going the way of Albatross, their ancestor who killed many dragons long ago.

parts.text: If that was true,
parts.meaning: If that was right,

parts.text: the same thing could be happening to Anemone
parts.meaning: Anemone might be changing in the same way

parts.text: that happened to Albatross, their murderous ancestor all those centuries ago.
parts.meaning: as Albatross, the ancestor who became a killer long ago.

sentences.grammar: "The same thing… that happened to…" compares two dragons. "Could be happening" shows a possibility now.

sentences.context: He found a rip current moving swiftly east and slipped into it, spreading his wings to catch as much of its speed as possible.
sentences.simple: Turtle found a fast current going east, got into it, and spread his wings to go as fast as he could.
sentences.main: Turtle uses the sea to travel fast.

parts.text: He found a rip current moving swiftly east
parts.meaning: He found a strong current flowing quickly east

parts.text: and slipped into it,
parts.meaning: and moved into it,

parts.text: spreading his wings to catch as much of its speed as possible.
parts.meaning: opening his wings to use as much of its speed as he could.

sentences.grammar: "As much… as possible" means the most you can. A "rip current" is a strong current in the sea.

sentences.context: Killing Queen Coral was one thing — that was the only way for the next queen to take the throne, so every princess grew up with that possibility in her mind.
sentences.simple: Killing the queen was expected, since that was how a new queen took over, so every princess thought about it.
sentences.main: Killing the queen is the princesses' way.

parts.text: Killing Queen Coral was one thing
parts.meaning: Killing Queen Coral was something different

parts.text: — that was the only way for the next queen to take the throne,
parts.meaning: — it was the only way for a new queen to rule,

parts.text: so every princess grew up with that possibility in her mind.
parts.meaning: so every princess grew up thinking about it.

sentences.grammar: "X was one thing" means X is different from (and more normal than) what comes next.

sentences.context: Another night passed in flying, and the next morning Turtle found himself over the ocean, sunlight sparkling on waves as blue as Tsunami’s scales.
sentences.simple: Turtle flew all night, and in the morning he was over the sea, where sunlight shone on blue waves.

parts.text: Another night passed in flying,
parts.meaning: He flew through another night,

parts.text: and the next morning Turtle found himself over the ocean,
parts.meaning: and the next morning he was over the sea,

parts.text: sunlight sparkling on waves as blue as Tsunami’s scales.
parts.meaning: with sunlight shining on waves as blue as Tsunami.

sentences.grammar: "Found himself" means discovered that he was somewhere. The last part describes the scene.

sentences.context: Where all the tribes of Pyrrhia will learn to hug out their problems, of course, said Fin, grinning like a comedic barracuda.
sentences.simple: Fin joked that it was a school where tribes solve problems by hugging, grinning widely.

parts.text: Where all the tribes of Pyrrhia will learn to hug out their problems, of course,
parts.meaning: A place where all tribes learn to fix problems with hugs, of course,

parts.text: said Fin, grinning like a comedic barracuda.
parts.meaning: said Fin with a big funny grin.

sentences.grammar: Fin speaks in Aquatic, so there are no quotation marks. "Hug out" is a joke, like "talk out".

sentences.context: Somehow he’d expected to confront Anemone deep underwater, or in the rain; this idyllic beach scene didn’t fit his idea of an animus showdown.
sentences.simple: Turtle thought he would face Anemone underwater or in the rain; a lovely beach didn't seem right for a magic battle.

parts.text: Somehow he’d expected to confront Anemone deep underwater, or in the rain;
parts.meaning: He had thought he would face Anemone deep in the sea or in the rain;

parts.text: this idyllic beach scene didn’t fit his idea of an animus showdown.
parts.meaning: this perfect, peaceful beach didn't match his idea of a magic fight.

sentences.grammar: The semicolon contrasts what he expected with what he found. "Showdown" means a final fight.

sentences.context: The sand erupted as hundreds of crabs came swarming out of their burrows, from tiny hermit crabs up to massive talon-sized red monsters with snapping claws.
sentences.simple: Hundreds of crabs burst out of the sand, from tiny ones to big red ones with snapping claws.

parts.text: The sand erupted
parts.meaning: The sand burst open

parts.text: as hundreds of crabs came swarming out of their burrows,
parts.meaning: as hundreds of crabs rushed out of their holes,

parts.text: from tiny hermit crabs up to massive talon-sized red monsters with snapping claws.
parts.meaning: from tiny hermit crabs to huge red ones with snapping claws.

sentences.grammar: "From… up to…" shows a range from smallest to biggest.

sentences.context: She was gone so quickly that Turtle thought he might have hallucinated her — that perhaps she was a double image accidentally reflected by the teleporting cracks.
sentences.simple: She vanished so fast that Turtle thought he might have imagined her, or seen a reflection in the magic cracks.

parts.text: She was gone so quickly
parts.meaning: She disappeared so fast

parts.text: that Turtle thought he might have hallucinated her
parts.meaning: that Turtle thought he had only imagined her

parts.text: — that perhaps she was a double image accidentally reflected by the teleporting cracks.
parts.meaning: — or maybe she was a reflection made by the magic cracks.

sentences.grammar: "So… that…" shows a result. "Might have + past participle" shows a possibility in the past.

sentences.context: He wasn’t defending his kingdom with valiant strength, and he might still be the idiot who died while the real heroes saved the day.
sentences.simple: Turtle wasn't bravely defending his home, and he might still be the foolish one who dies while the real heroes win.
sentences.main: This isn't the hero story he dreamed of.

parts.text: He wasn’t defending his kingdom with valiant strength,
parts.meaning: He wasn't bravely protecting his kingdom,

parts.text: and he might still be the idiot who died
parts.meaning: and he might still be the fool who died

parts.text: while the real heroes saved the day.
parts.meaning: while the true heroes won.

sentences.grammar: "Save the day" means solve the big problem. "While" means "at the same time as".

sentences.context: And far to the north, in the Ice Kingdom, in the midst of a blizzard, Winter’s brother Hailstorm stood before the wall of rankings, shivering with fever.
sentences.simple: Far north in the Ice Kingdom, during a snowstorm, Hailstorm stood sick in front of the wall of rankings.

parts.text: And far to the north, in the Ice Kingdom, in the midst of a blizzard,
parts.meaning: And far north, in the Ice Kingdom, in the middle of a snowstorm,

parts.text: Winter’s brother Hailstorm stood before the wall of rankings,
parts.meaning: Winter's brother Hailstorm stood in front of the rankings wall,

parts.text: shivering with fever.
parts.meaning: shaking because he was sick.

sentences.grammar: The sentence begins with three place and time phrases. "Shivering with fever" describes him.

a bunch of.meaning: A lot of; a group of.
a bunch of.example: He read a bunch of scrolls, fixed Flame’s face, made talismans to protect
a bunch of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

a couple of.example: of caring about some other dragons and trying to do a couple of little things to help them, and where did that lead him?
a couple of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

about to.meaning: Going to happen or do something very soon.

at the moment.example: And it certainly helped that everyone had a much bigger, flashier dragon on their minds at the moment.

right now.example: He felt a small pang of guilt at the crushing despair on the dragonet's face — but his anger was too strong to hold back right now.

a little bit.example: The princes glanced at one another nervously, and then one of them paddled forward a little bit.

hold on.meaning: To wait a moment, or to grip tight and not let go.
hold on.example: He shuddered, and his hold on the coral loosened, and it darted forward in a flash and bopped Queen Glory on the side of her tail.

let go.meaning: To stop holding someone or something.
let go.example: Startled, he let go, and the earring confidently made a beeline straight for Turtle's ear

would rather.meaning: Would prefer. You want one choice more than another.
would rather.example: Those who would rather follow Darkstalker to the old kingdom are free to go.”

on the other talon.meaning: In this story, the dragon way of saying on the other hand. It introduces a different idea.
on the other talon.example: On the other talon, 'something is coming to shake the earth' — that's totally me! Watch this.” He stomped one foot on the ground so hard that tremors shuddered out in all directions
